If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does:
  - It builds a Java String from the UTF-8 bytes of the supplementary Unicode character U+1D362 (COUNTING ROD UNIT DIGIT THREE).
  - It calls StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml on that String.
  - It asserts the escaped output equals the single numeric entity for the code point: "𝍢".

- Call path in the SUT:
  - StringEscapeUtils.escapeHtml(String) delegates to escapeHtml(Writer, String), which calls Entities.HTML40.escape(writer, string).
  - Entities.escape(Writer, String) performs the actual escaping by iterating over the string’s characters.

- Core implementation behavior causing the bug:
  - Entities.escape(Writer, String) loops over the string using charAt(i) and processes one 16-bit char at a time:
    - It looks up a named entity for the char; if none and the char is > 0x7F, it writes a decimal numeric entity for that 16-bit char:
      - writer.write("&#");
      - writer.write(Integer.toString(c, 10));
      - writer.write(';');
  - For supplementary characters (code points > U+FFFF), Java represents them as a surrogate pair (two char values). The current code treats each surrogate unit independently and emits two numeric entities for the surrogate halves (e.g., “��”), instead of combining them into a single code point numeric entity (“𝍢”).

- Why the test fails:
  - The test expects escapeHtml to produce a single numeric entity for U+1D362: "𝍢".
  - Because Entities.escape processes 16-bit chars rather than full Unicode code points, it emits two entities for the high and low surrogate units, producing an incorrect result that does not match "𝍢".

- Summary:
  - The bug is in Entities.escape(Writer, String): it is not surrogate-aware. It must detect a high-surrogate followed by a low-surrogate, compute the actual code point via Character.toCodePoint(high, low), write a single numeric entity for that code point, and advance the loop to skip the low surrogate. Currently, it writes numeric entities for each surrogate unit separately, leading to the observed failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
